newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. envoy flies to Kabul for talks with Taleban.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy flies to Kabul for talks with Taleban.

text.p: The United Nations special envoy to Afghanistan left for Kabul on Sunday for talks with leaders of the radical Islamic Taleban movement, a U.N. official said.
The official said Norbert Holl was expected to meet acting Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammed Ghous, but did not know if he would have talks with any other Taleban leaders.
Holl has been trying to prevent any military confrontation between the Taleban and Uzbek militia leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, who controls six northern provinces.
He has also conveyed U.N. concerns about human rights and the treatment of women under the Taleban administration, which has issued a series of edicts to enforce Islamic sharia law.

Holl visited Dostum in northern Afghanistan on Thursday and also met Ghous in Kabul, but a planned session with the Taleban's interim shura (council) leader Mullah Mohammed Rabbani did not take place.
Dostum and the Taleban, whose forces are face to face just south of the strategic Salang Tunnel about 90 km (60 miles) north of Kabul, have said they do not want to fight.
The Taleban, who swept into Kabul on September 27, have sworn to impose a strict Islamic order on all of Afghanistan, in contrast to Dostum's relatively liberal administration.

For the moment, the Sunni Moslem militants are concentrating their efforts on trying to drive forces loyal to former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood from their Panjsher Valley stronghold northeast of Kabul.
Taleban sources in Pakistan said the Panjsher frontline was calm on Sunday after heavy fighting on Saturday in which the Taleban captured two hills at the entrance to the valley.
The sources, quoted by the Afghan Islamic Press agency, said 15 of Masood's fighters had been killed and nine captured in the battle, while the Taleban suffered only two wounded.
The agency quoted independent sources as saying that at least four Taleban fighters had been killed and 12 wounded.
